source: https://github.com/tristan-f-r/npm-rank raw.json (top 10000 by popularity), randomly shuffled with a fixed seed (42), first 300 draws taken then de-duplicated by name.
description: Random sample of real npm packages used to pick Phase 4 thresholds empirically. IMPORTANT caveat: the source dataset itself contains only 5247 truly unique package names among its 10000 ranked entries (250 names are repeated, up to 21 times, apparently a scraping artifact upstream) — so a naive 300-item draw yielded only 270 unique packages after de-duplication. This is the de-duplicated set. Each entry was analyzed by calling the real production functions in src/versionAnomalyCheck.js directly (getVersionHistory/checkDormancy/checkMajorJump/checkMaintainerChange) at multiple candidate thresholds, not a reimplementation, so these numbers cannot drift from what the shipped code actually does.
